findings.text: The plan's section 4 states the selector composes with the existing traversal: 'source_rank then counts the leaf and the struct levels below it, and _struct_array_positions and the preserved-position rule apply to those levels as today.' All four new tests set source_rank=1, which for the ragged synthetic store (positions coil and element) leaves structural_rank 0 and preserved_positions empty, so no test exercises struct_array_entry together with a preserved position below the selected level (structural_rank >= 1, where positions[-structural_rank:] must name only levels below the consumed first struct array). The implementation reads as correct for that case -- it consumes index positions[0] and preserves the deepest levels -- but the composition the plan asserts is untested, so a future change to positions/preserved could break it silently. Not a defect; a coverage gap.

When a binding declares struct_array_entry but the first struct array on its dd_path is present yet empty, _struct_array_positions (line 183-184) raises a bare KeyError('/'.join(components)) before the new 'holds no struct array to select an entry from' BindingTransformError can speak, and _NetCDFStoreArrays.read catches only OSError, so the caller sees a KeyError rather than the TransformEngineError/BindingTransformError family the plan names for this slot. The new guard fires only when there is no struct array at all, not when the array is empty. The JT-60SA store's coils are non-empty (element counts 6..40), so this is unreachable for the binding the slot was added for; recorded as a robustness note, not a defect.

follow_ons: The two tests/data/test_machine_map.py failures (test_every_binding_targets_a_writable_shape_compatible_dd_leaf, test_every_mast_map_range_is_one_geometry_transition) are pytest-timeout (>300s) reads of a large MAST zarr consolidated-metadata JSON on GPFS, reproduce identically at the base revision, and are outside this node's declared write scope; raising the pytest timeout or caching that read is a separate node's work (declared by the reviewed run).

The catalogue node that consumes this slot is next: imas_ambix/data/machine_maps/jt-60sa.json declares one binding family and one structure assembly per pf_active coil, each binding carrying struct_array_entry by coil name, and must declare source_rank so structural_rank counts only the levels below the consumed first struct array (the composition untested here, finding 1).
The empty-first-struct-array case (finding 2) would be worth a guard if any future static store can carry an empty struct array.

justifications: Independent review of run r-20261006T022627509647-jtmm-static-entry-selector (plan imas-ambix:jt60sa-machine-map section 4), reviewed_base_sha e092f8ab7513407d50fa44983c4f02346b531b6b, reviewed_head_sha 97cc0dd6c3aa284f5a72fea5fb9cce507d821f35, stored as a parsed record scoring all six dimensions in 0..20 -- goal_fidelity 19, evidence 19, scope_discipline 20, durability 18, fit 19, reuse 20 -- total 115/120, added_failure_count 0 with added_failure_ids []. The node implements section 4's engine repair faithfully: an optional struct_array_entry binding slot lets a static netCDF binding read one named entry of the first struct array on its dd_path, which is exactly the per-coil reach the plan's repair names, and the twelve real OP1 coils read as element lengths [40,40,40,40,16,16,16,16,16,16,6,6]. Scope is clean (five declared files, no data artefacts touched). Durability is the weakest dimension only because the selector-plus-preserved-position composition the plan asserts is untested (finding 1) and the shared MAST-zarr read still times out at the base (a declared out-of-scope follow-on); the four new tests do carry a guard that fires, which I reproduced. Fit and reuse are strong: the change extends the existing _read_ids_path traversal and the existing error family rather than adding a parallel path, threaded by a defaulted dataclass field that leaves every existing binding unchanged, and it adds no machine-name branch. Two follow-on findings recorded, neither a regression.
